data.narrative:
Sila Nanotechnologies is a late-stage private company in Climate & Energy that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The comparable universe includes nine peers in the sector: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the narrow peer set—filtered for same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to support a reliable peer-median multiple approach, making direct comparable company analysis inapplicable at this time.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology applied to the $1.3B total raised proxy. A typical late-stage step-up multiplier of 1.2x implies a valuation of $1.6B. This single-method triangulation produces a range of $1.3B (floor, using raised capital directly) to $1.8B (ceiling, applying a modest 38% premium to the raised base), with $1.6B as the median point estimate.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.8B, centered near $1.6B. Material uncertainties remain: the sparse late-stage Climate & Energy comparables limit cross-validation, and the absence of disclosed revenue or burn metrics prevents DCF or revenue-multiple grounding. Additional disclosure of financial performance or a tighter peer valuation dataset would materially strengthen conviction in any point within this range.
